findings.why: Announced in the PR description: "New usernames can be at most 32 characters (was 64), so they fit the new profile layout.". The diff changes the username validation max length from 64 to 32, causing POST /api/users to return 400 for usernames longer than 32 characters.

suspicions.claim: User registration with username longer than 32 characters now fails with validation error instead of succeeding
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/users with JSON body containing username of 33+ characters (e.g., 'a'*33), valid email, and password. Read response status code (expect 400) and error message about username length.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s1 POST /api/users with 33-char username returned base 201 (success) and head 400 with error 'Length must be between 3 and 32.'

suspicions.claim: Authenticated user cannot update their own username to 33+ characters via PUT /api/me
suspicions.trigger: First POST /api/tokens with basic auth to get access token. Then PUT /api/me with Authorization: Bearer <token> and JSON body containing username of 33+ characters. Read response status code (expect 400) and validation error.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s2 PUT /api/me with 33-char username returned base 200 (success) and head 400 with error 'Length must be between 3 and 32.'

suspicions.claim: OAuth2 user creation may fail if provider returns username longer than 32 characters
suspicions.trigger: Mock OAuth2 provider to return username of 33+ characters in user info response. Complete OAuth2 flow with valid code/state. Read response status code (expect 400 or 500) and error indicating username validation failure.
suspicions.evidence: OAuth2 flow did not complete: GET /api/tokens/oauth2/github returned HTML login page, POST /api/tokens/oauth2/github returned 401/401; no request reached user creation with long username from provider.

suspicions.claim: Database schema still allows 64-character usernames creating inconsistency between API validation and storage layer
suspicions.trigger: Not directly testable via HTTP API. Would require direct database insertion of 33-64 character username to verify schema permits it while API rejects it.
suspicions.evidence: Not testable via HTTP API; requires direct database insertion which probes did not perform.

suspicions.claim: Existing users with usernames 33-64 characters (created before this change) may experience issues with profile layout or API responses
suspicions.trigger: If any pre-existing users have 33-64 char usernames, retrieve them via GET /api/users/<id> or authenticated GET /api/me. Verify response includes full username without truncation but profile layout may break (visual issue not API-testable).
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users and GET /api/me returned same users (alice, bob, carol) with short usernames in both base and head; no pre-existing 33-64 char username users were present or retrieved.
